meta.title: "Loud, emotional… but where are the facts?" — how to teach your child to spot empty rhetoric | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to ask one simple question — "where are the facts?" — and stop mistaking confidence for truth. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: Your child hears a confident, emotional speech — and already believes it's true?
hero.subheadline: "This is the best!", "this is a disaster!", "everyone normal has already done it!". Strong words, a confident voice — and that's enough. Your child reacts to the delivery, not the content.

media.alt: A child captivated by a loud, emotional speech that contains no facts

pain.title: Lots of emotion, lots of words — and not a single fact
pain.body:
Your child hears a confident, emotional speech — and it feels true. "This is the best!", "this is a disaster!", "everyone normal has already done it!" — at school, online, in videos. Strong words, a confident voice — and that's enough to believe it.

But these aren't arguments — it's empty rhetoric. Lots of words, lots of emotion — but not a single fact. It sounds convincing, yet it proves nothing. The child reacts to the delivery, not the content.

Without the skill to spot it, the child mistakes confidence for truth. The result — they agree with something that was never even backed up. Not because they're "gullible", but because reacting to emotion is natural.

solution.body: 50 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to defend themselves with words.
bullets: 🔍 Tells confident delivery apart from a real argument
❓ Asks one simple question — "where are the facts?" — and looks for the basis behind the words

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
